summary: How RF harms people and the FCC exposure rules, then lightning, power tools, electrical fires and shock.

blocks.title: RF and the body
items: RF, radio frequency energy, weakens quickly with distance from the antenna.
Power density, what limits measure: RF energy through each small patch of area every second.
Heat is the harm. Water in tissue warms as the wave twists it. Blood carries heat away, until RF heats faster than blood can cool.

blocks.title: FCC exposure limits
items: MPE, Maximum Permissible Exposure: the highest RF power density allowed, set well below the level of harm.
MPE limits are in FCC Part 1. OET Bulletin 65 (Office of Engineering and Technology) explains how to check a site.
Exposure is averaged over time: short bursts are fine if the average stays under the limit.
Controlled: workers who know the RF is there. Uncontrolled: the general public, with stricter limits.

blocks.title: Lightning
items: Lightning takes the easiest path to earth, so a tall mast is the likely strike point.
A strike, even nearby, sends a surge along feed lines and power wires.
Grounding: heavy wire gives surges an easy way down.
Bonding: all station metal tied together, so current won't jump between parts.
Surge protector: opens a path to ground on a spike.
No device protects against a direct hit. These only limit damage.

blocks.title: Workbench
items: Power drill: always wear eye protection, even in an extreme emergency.
Short circuit: an accidental shortcut around the load. Huge current overheats the wires: a Class C fire.
Electrical fire: use a non-conducting agent: carbon dioxide, dry chemical or clean-agent gas. Never water or foam. Turn off the breaker if you can.
Shock: current runs from a live wire through you to ground. Muscles clench; the heart can falter.
GFI, ground fault interrupter: prevents shock by comparing hot and neutral to sense ground path current. It shuts the circuit down at about 5 mA.

blocks.title: Exam traps
items: Short-circuit fire question: the choices are only codes. Pick FE30.
6 controlled, 30 uncontrolled. Not swapped, not 1 and 15.
RF eye harm is heat: not magnetic fields, a polarized lens or attracted metal.
Antenna share: 5%, not 1% or 12.5%. Study: 1000 W, not 500 W or 100 W.
A lightning protector, grounded cabinet or short lead-in won't stop a direct hit.
Stubs work only at their tuned band, not all frequencies.
